newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says to sign Paris Club documents soon.
newsitem.headline: Russia says to sign Paris Club documents soon.

text.p: Russia will sign admission papers with the Paris Club of country creditors within a few months, Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Monday.
"It is clear that in the next few months...Russia will join the Paris Club as a country-creditor," Kasyanov told a news conference.

He said Paris Club representatives had agreed to Russia's insistence that the former Soviet Union's credit which Russia inherited was to be calculated at the State Bank of the Soviet Union's rate of 0.60 roubles per dollar.
The rate and the discount to which the debt to Russia is to be subject were the main stumbling blocks in the talks between Russia and the Paris Club.
Russia and the Paris Club reached a principal agreement on Russia's entry to the Club before the Group of Seven industrialised nations meeting last week in Denver.
Russia is seeking repayment on $37 billion of debt inherited from the Soviet Union from poorer nations, which have agreements with the Paris Club.
Kasyanov said the amount of the discount would be calculated in two weeks.
